subject: Garrison, for your MCP gateway survey
body_text:
> Hi Daniel,
> 
> I read your Q1 survey of MCP aggregation gateways and wanted to point you to one that is not in it: Garrison, a macOS menu bar app I built that runs each MCP server once and lets every client on the machine share it over loopback HTTP.
> 
> It is macOS only and does not do namespaces or nested aggregation, so it will not match your target architecture. What it does cover from your criteria is tool-level controls (a per-profile write gate that leaves the mutating tools out of tools/list rather than refusing them), a separate revocable token per client, and a record of every call per client.
> 
> Credentials are Keychain items, there is no container runtime and no account. The source is public and the signed build is $14.99 with a 30-minute trial:
> 
> https://github.com/tlorimer/garrison
> 
> Would be great if you could consider it for the next edition,
> 
> Thanks,
> Thibault

subject: Your Lashon Hara Chatbot Project
body_text:
Bs”d

Shalom,

I recently came across your Lashon-Hara-Chatbot repository on GitHub while
looking into whether anyone has already explored using AI to help people
avoid lashon hara.

I realize the project may only have been an early experiment, but it caught
my attention because I’ve been thinking about a somewhat related idea: a
voluntary AI tool that could help people at the actual moment of online
communication—while writing or before sending a message, post, email,
comment, etc., and perhaps eventually with incoming communication as well.

The thought would be to ground it as much as possible in Sefer Chofetz
Chaim and develop it with proper rabbinic guidance, so that it could deal
not only with obviously negative language but also with questions of
context, to’eles, and when something may require asking a rav.

I’d be very interested to know what you had in mind when you started the
chatbot project, how far you took it, and whether you still have any
interest in this area.

I’m a writer rather than a programmer, and I’m not coming with funding or a
developed project. At this stage I’m mainly trying to understand what has
already been attempted, what might realistically be possible, and whether
there are people already thinking along similar lines whom it would make
sense to speak with rather than reinventing the wheel.

If you’d be open to a brief conversation, I’d be very glad to hear your
thoughts.

Kol tuv,

Ezra Yonah Feld

-- 



Check out my blog: https://quillmoorkitchen.wordpress.com/

subject: LumaVoice — another approach to offline dictation on Wayland
body_text: Hi Daniel!I came across your work on getting Handy running under Wayland, along with your other Linux voice typing projects. Looks like we've been tackling many of the same challenges.I've been developing LumaVoice, an open-source, offline speech-to-text application built specifically around Linux, GNOME and Wayland.It uses GTK4/libadwaita, supports Faster-Whisper and whisper.cpp, and provides system-wide dictation, model management, multilingual recognition, and spoken punctuation.GitHub: https://github.com/igor-melnikov/lumavoiceI noticed you've explored some of the same tricky areas, especially global shortcuts and text injection under Wayland.I'd be interested to hear your thoughts on the project, particularly whether you've found better ways to handle those limitations.If you feel it's relevant, I'd also be happy to contribute it to your Linux voice technology resource list.Cheers,Igor Melnikov

subject: your agent sessions category
body_text:
Hey Daniel,

Saw your Claude Code plugin marketplace. A whole QA & Agent Sessions
category tells me you've taxonomized this problem space pretty
thoroughly.

I'm building Tessaly, a Mac app for when you've got more Claude Code and
Codex runs going than you can keep track of. You start work, walk
away, and when you come back it tells you what finished, what's stuck
and what needs you. The persistent board those sessions were missing.

It's in private beta on Apple Silicon Macs. If you want in, put your
email in at trytessaly.com and I'll let you straight in.

Cheers,
Tobin
